hexFieldRepair.trigger: coordinator measurement after review, reproduced here: WebKit 26.5 reports no match for /^(?:[0-9a-f]{2})+$/ on valid input past 2,785,276 characters
hexFieldRepair.measuredWith: Playwright bundled engines, headless, this Mac; hex-engines-probe.cjs.txt run with node from the repository root

webkit26_5.groupedPattern: accepts 2,785,276 characters, refuses 2,785,278; false (no throw) at 4, 16, 32 and 64 MiB of characters in 58 to 78 ms
webkit26_5.groupedPatternWithJSC_useJIT_false: same threshold; the environment variable did not demonstrably disable the JIT (a 2e7 loop took 9 ms)
webkit26_5.flatPattern: true at 64 MiB of characters, 44 to 45 ms
webkit26_5.characterCodeDecoder: correct at 64 MiB of characters, 79 to 80 ms; refuses bad start, middle, end, odd length and uppercase

chromium151.groupedPattern: true at 64 MiB of characters, 37 ms

firefox153.groupedPattern: true at 64 MiB of characters, 35 ms

releasedBehaviourOnWebKit.baseline: encodeLocalBaseline's self-decode throws plain Error('Invalid inbound frame') (no code) for any field over about 1.39 MB of bytes: snapshot, history record, receipt or carried source capsule. planLocalRetention rethrows it (not LocalBaselineCapacityError, not LocalBaselineError), so automatic maintenance halts as owner-error ('stopped because a storage or verification check failed'), not a capacity park. Planning is a dry run: nothing is reserved, sealed or written, and the storage job runner closes the session only for repair-required or generation-changed codes, so sync continues. Reopening retries and halts again.
releasedBehaviourOnWebKit.releasedSnapshotWindow: about 1.39 MB to 2.0 MiB of snapshot halts; larger snapshots park as capacity because the 4 MiB length check runs before the self-decode
releasedBehaviourOnWebKit.phase542AsReviewed: every field over about 1.39 MB halts up to the 32 MiB ceiling, so 2 to 16 MiB snapshots that the released code parked would halt instead
releasedBehaviourOnWebKit.ownerProbe: webkit-owner-probe.ts.txt: with the grouped pattern emulated, a real owner's removeHistory rejected with Error('Invalid inbound frame') at 1.6 MiB and 2.25 MiB of text; the counter stayed v2 with no chunk keys. Without emulation both reduced.
releasedBehaviourOnWebKit.otherPathsOnWebKit: spool and delivery wires (2 MiB bound) and legacy inbound record pages (4 MiB record, 10 MiB page bound) used the same pattern; spool and delivery refusals are repair-required ContentErrors, which close the session. Currently admitted envelopes are at most 512 KiB, so only historical or multi-envelope inputs could reach the threshold.
